lesson_title: Practice Paper Run: Every Mark Accounted For
hook_text: Borrow R750 000. Repay R1 981 500. The exam question hiding a life lesson about interest.
clip_script: A loan of seven hundred and fifty thousand rand is repaid over three hundred equal monthly payments at nine comma six percent per annum compounded monthly. The formula: P equals x times, one minus one plus i to the minus n, over i. The monthly rate: nought comma zero zero eight. The payment lands at six thousand six hundred and four rand and ninety-four cents. Now multiply by three hundred: about one comma nine eight million rand — more than double the amount borrowed. That comparison sentence is a favourite final subquestion, and the interest alone is one comma two three million.
visual_style: A house-shaped stack of banknotes on one side of a balance scale; each monthly payment slides across as a note until the repaid pile towers to more than double the house, the interest portion glowing a different colour.
mood: Jaw-drop consumer maths — the exam question that doubles as financial literacy.
pacing: Calm formula setup, rhythmic payment ticker accelerating, hard stop on the 1,98 million reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full practice run and walk the whole paper with every mark accounted for.
